note: P-258 LANE-C ADDENDUM (2026-09-16, acquisition campaign, branch seat/p258-lane-c) -- THIS FILE HAD NO NOTE BEFORE THIS PASS; it now has one, because this pass found that the City of Bastrop has REPLACED ITS ZONING CODE and the ten rows above are from the retired instrument. WHAT WAS HERE: R-MD, R-LD, R-HD, P, CMU, C-1, C-2, I-1, I-2 and DT-1, coded from the pre-2026 City of Bastrop Code of Ordinances (Municode). Those names are the OLD scheme and do not appear in the code in force. WHAT IS IN FORCE NOW: the Bastrop Development Code, adopted by Ordinance No. 2026-06, which repeals the former B3 Code and becomes Chapter 14 of the Code of Ordinances; its roster is P/OS, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, MU, GC, PI, IND and PDD. The city GIS zoning layer has already migrated -- the lane-c codes this file was missing (GC 588 parcels, MU 326, PI 100, IND 70, P/OS 35) are EXACTLY that new roster, which is the evidence for the migration. THE OLDER ROWS ARE LEFT IN PLACE, NOT DELETED, and are KNOWN-STALE NAMES: deleting or renaming them is a judgement for the table owners, not for this lane. They also carry no per-value provenance, which is why this table is (and stays) the legacy un-gated county table. WHY NO ROWS WERE ADDED HERE, AND WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR THESE FIVE CODES. Read the ordinance first, then the wiring. (1) THE ORDINANCE. The adopted ordinance PDF at cityofbastrop.org (ORDINANCE NO. 2026-06, read 2026-09-16) does carry Dimensional Standards Charts for exactly these districts, and this pass read them: GC -- front 20, side 5, corner-side street 10, rear 20, height 55 ft (5 stories), maximum impervious 65 pct; MU -- GENERAL MU DEVELOPMENT chart front 15, side 5 (0 allowed on shared/party-wall sides within a unified development; 10 where abutting RR or SF), corner-side street 10, rear 15, impervious 60 pct, and the district has a SEPARATE ATTACHED-RESIDENTIAL chart giving rear 10 (15 abutting RR/SF) and height 40 ft / 3 stories where the general chart gives 45 ft / 4 stories; PI -- front 25 (may be reduced to 10 for urban frontage with fire access and pedestrian facilities), side 15, corner-side street 20, rear 20, height 55 ft (5 stories), impervious 65 pct; IND -- front 25, side 20 (40 abutting a residential district), corner-side street 20, rear 25 (40 abutting residential), height 60 ft (5 stories), impervious 65 pct; P/OS -- front, side, rear and corner-side street all None (15 ft where abutting a residential district), height 35 ft, impervious None with a drainage-compliance requirement. Those are real chart scalars, not invented numbers, and THAT FALSIFIES PART OF THE PRIOR RATIONALE: the honest-decline recorded in bastrop-development-code.json says these districts have no chart rows because their standards are conditional/contextual -- the conditionality is real (abutting-district escalations, overlay adjustments, two charts for MU), but a base scalar DOES exist for each of the five. (2) THE WIRING. These codes do not read from this file at all. lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts routes the bastrop-tx key plus any known BDC stamp to the bastrop-development-code table (isKnownBdcDistrictCode covers MU/GC/PDD/PI/IND/OS and P-OS), and only genuinely non-BDC codes (R-MD and the rest of the retired county scheme) fall through to this table. Rows written here would therefore never be served to a GC/MU/PI/IND/P-OS parcel. (3) THE LOCK. bastrop-development-code.json is hash-locked byte-for-byte against a mirror lock in hauska-engine (WDLL 2026-07-29 BDC STEP 3; bastropDevelopmentCodeSetbackHashLock.test.ts pins SHA256 18b9bca9...), and bastropDevelopmentCodeSetbacks.test.ts asserts positively that MU/GC/PDD have NO row in it. Adding rows to that table from this lane would break a cross-repo content lock whose other half lives in a repository this lane does not touch, and would silently invert a decision that has its own test. THIS PASS THEREFORE WITHDREW the five rows it had briefly written into this file and records the chart values above AS EVIDENCE INSTEAD OF AS ROWS, so the finding is not lost. FOR THE TABLE OWNERS: promoting these five codes is a policy change, not a research gap -- it needs (a) a decision that the BDC flat table should carry base scalars with the conditional cases quoted, (b) rows added to bastrop-development-code.json, and (c) the SHA256 lock updated in BOTH repos. Until then these lane-c units honest-decline, which is the behaviour CORRECTION C intended. EFFECTIVE DATE -- RECORDED HONESTLY AS NOT READ: the ordinance PDF cover page OCRs as mirrored text, so no legible adoption or effective-date clause could be extracted; the ordinance number (2026-06) and the City own 2026-02-03 executive summary (which still describes the code as conditional on adoption) are the only dating evidence this pass has. Do NOT treat 2026-04-14 from the neighbouring BDC table note as re-verified here. SOURCES TRIED: the City adopted ordinance PDF (READ -- source of every value quoted above); the City Draft 2026 Bastrop Development Code PDF at cityofbastrop.org/upload/page/0047/docs (read; same charts, confirms the roster); the City Development Code executive summary PDF (read; dating evidence); two City Council meeting packets on mccmeetings.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net (read; confirm the GC/PI/IND/P/OS names and SF-1/GC/PI conversions in live rezoning items); Municode (the older cited source; not re-fetched this pass). ArcGIS REST not queried: the gap was ordinance text, and the layer codes were already in hand from the worklist.
